How to Prepare for Your Kitchen Measurement and 3D Design: A Checklist

Key takeaways

  • Have your appliance list and model numbers ready; they decide the cabinet sizes.
  • Collect a few photos of kitchens you like, and note what you dislike about your current one.
  • Know your must-haves for storage and a comfortable budget range; the 3D design does the rest.

Before the visit

  • Appliances: list every appliance with model numbers, including ones you plan to buy.
  • Inspiration: save 5 to 10 photos of kitchens you like; screenshots are fine.
  • Pain points: write down what does not work in your current kitchen.
  • Storage: list what must fit, such as trash and recycling, spices, pots, small appliances, and a pantry.
  • Budget: a comfortable range helps the designer suggest the right materials from the start.

During the measurement

We measure walls, ceiling height, windows, doors, and the positions of plumbing, gas, and outlets. Clear the counters and the area under the sink if you can, so nothing is hidden. Mention anything you plan to move, such as a wall, a window, or the range.

Reviewing your 3D design

You see your own room in 3D, with your door style, colors, and hardware. Two rounds of design changes are included in the price, so take your time. Open every drawer in your head: where do the plates go, where does the trash go, where will you cook?

Questions to ask

  • What is included in the quote, and what is not?
  • When does production start, and when will installation happen?
  • What does the warranty cover?
  • Who is my contact during the project?
